verdictRationale: The production implementation (Python service, routes, 0068 SQL/role/grants/RLS, schema additions, frontend helper/panel/approval display and AC11 pin chain) satisfies the six frozen R1 amendments on every point I traced, and I found no production code defect. One R1-TRUST-required proof is not delivered: the definer direct-call negative tests for missing subject context and cross-tenant context never reach those guards, and append_first_workspace_intent has no direct-call negative test at all, so deleting its SQL-side closed-shape/CPU/GPU/target guards would fail no behavioral test (only the repinnable catalogue hash). The fix is test-only and bounded. ACCEPT_FIRST_WORKSPACE_R1_CODE_KEEP_REAL_DEPLOYMENT_GATES is not issued until that proof exists at an exact SHA with hosted Core/Backend success.

mandatoryCodeDefects.failedInvariant: R1-TRUST requires direct-call, missing-context and cross-tenant tests against the SECURITY DEFINER helpers; Root catalogue decision lists the helper-side rechecks (current epoch/kill switch, requester/project linkage, ready Workspace, current intent/versions/hash) as required security properties. A test that cannot fail when a guard is removed does not prove that guard.
mandatoryCodeDefects.causalExample: The loop sets inv.tenant_id (and, in case 2, inv.first_workspace_subject) but never sets inv.first_workspace_epoch. Both cases therefore raise at the first guard (0068 SQL lines 48-51, 'Current epoch and tenant admission required'), so the 'missing subject' (lines 52-53) and 'cross-tenant' paths are never reached. Separately, append_first_workspace_intent is reached only through create_intent after Python validate_contract/_validate have already rejected oversize CPU, GPU, extra keys and wrong target. Mutation check: delete the GPU/cpuMillis/memory/closed-key/target-membership predicates at SQL lines 65-99. No behavioral test fails. Only the catalogue definitionSHA256 pin notices, and that pin is mechanically repinned under the bounded-correction rule (as already happened in this series). Meanwhile an inv_kernel connection with the GUCs set could insert a GPU or oversized workload through the definer owner's INSERT grant.
mandatoryCodeDefects.boundedFix: Test-only; no production, SQL, migration or definer-hash change. (a) In the existing loop, set inv.first_workspace_epoch to the current epoch so each case reaches its own guard, and assert the specific exception text (missing subject -> 'Verified service context required'; subject of tenant A with inv.tenant_id=other -> refused before any write). (b) Add direct-call negatives for inv.append_first_workspace_intent under the restricted runtime role with otherwise complete valid context, one property changed per case: gpuCount 1, cpuMillis 501, memoryBytes 8388607, an extra key such as workspaceStart, a canonical/sha mismatch, a non-ready or version-mismatched Workspace, a targetNodeId not enabled in project_nodes, and spec tenantId differing from inv.tenant_id. Each case asserts InsufficientPrivilege and unchanged workload counts. (c) Add equivalent direct-call negatives for append_first_workspace_run with full valid context and a stale workspace version, a stale workload version, a sha mismatch and a non-ready Workspace. Then publish a new exact SHA with hosted Core and Backend success; the AC11 definer/migration pins stay unchanged because the SQL bytes do not change.

rootPreDeployOperationalObligations: O1 Migration privilege: 0068 ALTERs function ownership to inv_first_workspace_writer, and its DO block refuses any pg_auth_members row for that role. Apply it as a superuser on the actual target PostgreSQL. A non-superuser CREATEROLE migrator cannot SET ROLE to the new owner, and on PG16+ CREATE ROLE would auto-grant the creator membership, which the safety check correctly refuses. Hosted CI proves only the superuser test path.

O2 Irreversible head: 0068.downgrade raises, so recovery is forward-fix only. Take a schema backup before apply. The AC11 migration-rehearsal reversible-segment axis may now report the workflow-accepted structural NOT_APPLICABLE (no-reversible-tail) at this head; treat that as expected, not as a regression or a pass.

O3 Packaging: redeploy the control-plane package (routes plus 0068 resource) and the web build together. Running PC2/3/4 Node images at 1efea need no redeploy for this change: node-agent Go code is unchanged, the embedded wire schema only gained additive definitions, and launch/approval/start wire shapes are unchanged (the existing optional WorkloadSpec.targetNodeId is used). The hosted execution test ran the 905-built Node, so compatibility with the live 1efea binary is inferred from the additive-only diff and still needs live confirmation.

O4 Runtime prerequisites for a non-refused list/create: a configured RestrictedWorkspaceRuntime whose Node is enabled in inv.project_nodes for the project; profile max memory at least 8388608 with at most 64 images and 64 executables (otherwise AUTH-0044 503); a genuinely ready Workspace via the existing admin path; business linkage (enabled business_projects, enabled business_subjects mapping to an active user, project_members role owner/maintainer/operator, kernel project_grants enabled+can_request); and a verified oidc:<64hex> subject.

O5 Fail-closed listing: any pre-existing workload whose spec.workspaceId equals the selected Workspace but is not a bounded CPU intent (GPU, extra keys, another target, digest drift) makes the whole first-intents list refuse (403/409), by R1 design. Inventory such rows before enabling the UI for a Workspace.

O6 Retained live gates, unchanged and not converted into code defects: protected API packages/dependencies/JWKS/private roots/separate restricted DSNs/provider/signer/TLS/policy/queue inventory/schema backup+apply; genuine ready Workspace and actual selected intent/Run; two real distinct non-requester approvals (extra real identity pending); Root same-origin portal migration under the main memory constraint; PC1 SSH publickey registration response; PC5 RAM/actual Linux VM Node/transport/sandbox/admission (Docker API 1.41 is supported by accepted minimum 1.41 / client ceiling 1.45); GPU/storage/physical resources/browser/renewal/tunnel reboot-reconnect/recovery/five-PC acceptance.

WorkspaceFirstProfile.minMemoryBytes const 8388608; WorkspaceFirstResources memory 8388608..67108864, cpu 1..500, gpu/minVram const 0; profile below 8MiB -> AUTH-0044 503 prerequisite; compile_launch still enforces the configured profile; generic ResourceRequest/WorkloadSpec unchanged (schema diff is additive-only; control-plane and node wire copies byte-identical to contracts).
amendmentFindings.R1-WIRE: Satisfied. Three paths and shapes as frozen; tenant/project/workspace/workload IDs and canonical SHA matched to row and context; requesterId oidc:[a-f0-9]{64}; ETag regexes are exact strong canonical base10 with lowercase hex and MAX_SAFE bound; If-Match added to the duplicate-header refusal set; Idempotency-Key via existing ASCII33..126/1..200 helper; Cache-Control no-store on all three routes; replay returns the stored original observedAt.
amendmentFindings.R1-LOCKS: Satisfied in source. Database.transaction sets tenant, epoch FOR SHARE and the tenant_controls barrier first; then Control.grant and business permission; then ledger INSERT ON CONFLICT + SELECT FOR UPDATE; then the Workspace FOR SHARE, project_nodes FOR SHARE and workload FOR SHARE locks with version/digest checks before the initial-vs-replay decision. Helper locks are reentrant re-acquisitions in the same order. One transaction covers inv.runs, public.runs, inv.business_runs, the outbox event and the ledger response, with rollback proven by the trigger-injection test. Same-key HTTP races (3x intent, 3x run) and replay-vs-first-prepare were run on real PG under the restricted role.
